# zentests

```go
import "github.com/kematzy/zentests"
```

Package zentests provides utilities for testing Go Fiber applications.

Basic usage:

```
func TestEndpoint(t *testing.T) {
    zt := zentests.New(t)
    zt.Get(app, "/users").Status(200)
}
```

<a name="CloseTestDB"></a>
## func CloseTestDB

```go
func CloseTestDB(t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB)
```

CloseTestDB explicitly closes the underlying database connection. In most tests this is not needed because [SetupTestDB](<#SetupTestDB>) registers an automatic close via [testing.T.Cleanup](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T.Cleanup>). Use this only when you need to close the connection before the test ends — for example, to verify reconnect behavior or to release a file\-based SQLite lock mid\-test.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB connection.

Example:

```
db := zentests.SetupTestDB(t)
// ... tests ...
zentests.CloseTestDB(t, db) // close early; t.Cleanup will be a no-op
```

<a name="DBCount"></a>
## func DBCount

```go
func DBCount[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, model *T, conditions ...any) int64
```

DBCount counts records matching the given conditions. Fails the test on database error.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- model: Pointer to model struct \(used only for type, can be &Model\{\}\).
- conditions: Optional \- pass a where string, then args. e.g., "status = ?", "active"

Returns:

- int64: The count of matching records.

Example:

```
count := zentests.DBCount(t, db, &User{})
s.Equal(int64(5), count)

count := zentests.DBCount(t, db, &User{}, "status = ?", "active")
```

<a name="DBCreate"></a>
## func DBCreate

```go
func DBCreate[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, record *T) *T
```

DBCreate saves a single record to the database and returns it with any auto\-populated fields \(ID, CreatedAt, etc.\) filled in. The test is failed immediately if the insert fails.

Type parameter T must be a GORM model struct; pass a pointer to an initialized value.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table already migrated.
- record: Pointer to the record to insert.

Returns:

- \*T: The same pointer, with auto\-generated fields populated by GORM.

Example:

```
user := zentests.DBCreate(t, db, &User{Name: "Alice", Email: "alice@example.com"})

s.NotZero(user.ID)      // ID populated after save
s.NotZero(user.CreatedAt)
```

<a name="DBCreateN"></a>
## func DBCreateN

```go
func DBCreateN[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, count int, factory func(i int) T) []*T
```

DBCreateN creates count records by calling factory once per record with a 1\-based index \(1, 2, … count\). Each record is inserted and returned with auto\-populated fields. The test is failed immediately if any insert fails.

The 1\-based index means you can use i directly in format strings without the i\+1 offset:

```
zentests.DBCreateN(t, db, 5, func(i int) User {
    return User{Email: fmt.Sprintf("user%d@example.com", i)} // user1, user2, ...
})
```

Type parameter T must be a GORM model struct \(not a pointer — the factory returns values; DBCreateN handles taking their address internally\).

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table already migrated.
- count: Number of records to create \(must be \> 0\).
- factory: Function called with i = 1..count; returns an initialized T value.

Returns:

- \[\]\*T: Slice of inserted record pointers, each with auto\-generated fields.

Example:

```
posts := zentests.DBCreateN(t, db, 3, func(i int) Post {
    return Post{Title: fmt.Sprintf("Post %d", i), Body: "content"}
})

s.Len(posts, 3)
s.Equal("Post 1", posts[0].Title)
```

## func DBDelete

```go
func DBDelete[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, record *T)
```

DBDelete deletes a record by ID and fails the test on error.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- record: Pointer to model struct with ID set.

Example:

```
user := &User{ID: 1}
zentests.DBDelete(t, db, user)
```

<a name="DBDeleteBy"></a>
## func DBDeleteBy

```go
func DBDeleteBy[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, model *T, where string, args ...any) int64
```

DBDeleteBy deletes records matching a where clause and fails the test on error.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- model: Pointer to model struct \(type used for table\).
- where: Where clause.
- args: Arguments for where clause.

Returns:

- int64: Number of records deleted.

Example:

```
deleted := zentests.DBDeleteBy(t, db, &User{}, "status = ?", "deleted")
```

<a name="DBExists"></a>
## func DBExists

```go
func DBExists[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, model *T, conditions ...any) bool
```

DBExists asserts that at least one record matches the given conditions. Fails the test if no records are found.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- model: Pointer to model struct \(type used for table\).
- conditions: Optional \- pass a where string, then args. e.g., "status = ?", "active"

Returns:

- bool: Always true if check passes.

Example:

```
s.True(zentests.DBExists(t, db, &User{}))
s.True(zentests.DBExists(t, db, &User{}, "status = ?", "active"))
```

<a name="DBFind"></a>
## func DBFind

```go
func DBFind[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, record *T, id any) *T
```

DBFind finds a record by ID and populates the result into the provided pointer. Fails the test if the record is not found or on database error. This is the idiomatic way to fetch a record by primary key in tests.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- record: Pointer to model struct to populate \(must be allocated\).
- id: The primary key value to find.

Returns:

- \*T: The same pointer, populated with the found record.

Example:

```
user := &User{}
zentests.DBFind(t, db, user, 1)
s.Equal("alice", user.Name)
```

<a name="DBFindBy"></a>
## func DBFindBy

```go
func DBFindBy[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, record *T, where string, args ...any) *T
```

DBFindBy finds a record by a specific field condition. Fails the test if exactly one record is not found or on error. Use this for non\-ID lookups \(e.g., by email, unique constraint\).

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- record: Pointer to model struct to populate.
- where: Where clause \(e.g., "email = ?" or "name LIKE ?"\).
- args: Arguments matching the where clause placeholders.

Returns:

- \*T: The same pointer, populated with the found record.

Example:

```
user := &User{}
zentests.DBFindBy(t, db, user, "email = ?", "alice@example.com")
s.Equal("Alice", user.Name)
```

<a name="DBFirst"></a>
## func DBFirst

```go
func DBFirst[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, record *T) *T
```

DBFirst retrieves the first record ordered by primary key. Fails the test if no records exist or on error. Use this when you need the oldest/first record by natural order.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- record: Pointer to model struct to populate.

Returns:

- \*T: The same pointer, populated with the first record.

Example:

```
user := &User{}
zentests.DBFirst(t, db, user)
s.Equal("Alice", user.Name) // first created user
```

<a name="DBLast"></a>
## func DBLast

```go
func DBLast[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, record *T) *T
```

DBLast retrieves the last record ordered by primary key \(descending\). Fails the test if no records exist or on error. Use this when you need the most recent record.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- record: Pointer to model struct to populate.

Returns:

- \*T: The same pointer, populated with the last record.

Example:

```
user := &User{}
zentests.DBLast(t, db, user)
s.Equal("Zoe", user.Name) // most recently created
```

<a name="DBMigrate"></a>
## func DBMigrate

```go
func DBMigrate(t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, models ...any)
```

DBMigrate runs GORM AutoMigrate for the provided models on an existing database. Use this when you have a DB from [SetupTestDB](<#SetupTestDB>) and want to add or update tables without recreating the connection.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB connection.
- models: One or more pointers to GORM model structs.

Example:

```
db := zentests.SetupTestDB(t)
zentests.DBMigrate(t, db, &User{}, &Post{})
```

<a name="DBNotExists"></a>
## func DBNotExists

```go
func DBNotExists[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, model *T, conditions ...any) bool
```

DBNotExists asserts that no records match the given conditions. Fails the test if any records are found.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- model: Pointer to model struct \(type used for table\).
- conditions: Optional \- pass a where string, then args, e.g. "email = ?", "deleted@example.com"

Returns:

```
bool: Always true if check passes.
```

Example:

```
s.True(zentests.DBNotExists(t, db, &User{}))
s.True(zentests.DBNotExists(t, db, &User{}, "email = ?", "deleted@example.com"))
```

<a name="DBReset"></a>
## func DBReset

```go
func DBReset(t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB)
```

DBReset deletes all rows from every table in the database and resets SQLite auto\-increment sequences, leaving the schema intact. This is faster than recreating the database and is the right tool for [testing.T.SetupTest](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T.SetupTest>) hooks in suites that share a single database connection across tests.

NOTE: This function is SQLite\-specific. The sequence reset step \(sqlite\_sequence\) is a no\-op on other databases but the DELETE statements will still clear data correctly on any GORM\-supported driver.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB connection.

Example:

```
func (s *MySuite) SetupTest() {
    zentests.DBReset(s.T(), s.db)
}
```

<a name="DBSeed"></a>
## func DBSeed

```go
func DBSeed[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, records []*T)
```

DBSeed loads test data from a map of slices \(table \-\> records\). This is useful for populating a database with test fixtures defined inline. Each key in data should be a pointer to a model struct; the value should be a slice of pointers to already\-populated model instances.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB.
- data: Map of model pointers to slices of populated records.

Example:

```
users := []*User{
    {Name: "Alice", Email: "alice@example.com"},
    {Name: "Bob", Email: "bob@example.com"},
}
posts := []*Post{
    {Title: "First Post", Body: "Hello world"},
}
zentests.DBSeed(t, db, users, posts)
```

<a name="DBSeedSlice"></a>
## func DBSeedSlice

```go
func DBSeedSlice[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, records []T)
```

DBSeedSlice loads test data from a slice of records. This is a convenience wrapper around DBSeed for single\-table seeding.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB.
- records: Slice of pointers to already\-populated model instances.

Example:

```
users := []*User{
    {Name: "Alice", Email: "alice@example.com"},
    {Name: "Bob", Email: "bob@example.com"},
}
zentests.DBSeedSlice(t, db, users)
```

<a name="DBTx"></a>
## func DBTx

```go
func DBTx(t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, fn func(tx *gorm.DB) error) error
```

DBTx executes a function within a transaction. The transaction is automatically rolled back if the function returns an error, otherwise it is committed when the function completes successfully. This is useful for testing multiple operations that should succeed or fail together.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB connection.
- fn: Function that executes operations on a transacted \*gorm.DB.

Returns:

- error: Any error returned by fn, which causes rollback.

Example:

```
err := zentests.DBTx(t, db, func(tx *gorm.DB) error {
    if err := tx.Create(&user).Error; err != nil {
        return err
    }
    return tx.Create(&balance).Error
})
s.NoError(err)
```

<a name="DBUpdate"></a>
## func DBUpdate

```go
func DBUpdate[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, model *T, byID any, updates map[string]any)
```

DBUpdate performs an update query and fails the test on error. Use this for simple field updates without loading the record first.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- model: Pointer to model struct \(used for table, must have ID if using byID\).
- byID: Primary key value to identify record; use nil for where clause.
- updates: Map of column to new value \(e.g., map\[string\]any\{"status": "inactive"\}\).

Example:

```
zentests.DBUpdate(t, db, &User{}, 1, map[string]any{"status": "inactive"})
```

<a name="DBUpdateBy"></a>
## func DBUpdateBy

```go
func DBUpdateBy[T any](t *testing.T, db *gorm.DB, model *T, where string, args []any, updates map[string]any)
```

DBUpdateBy performs an update using a where clause. Use this when you need to update records matching a non\-ID condition.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- db: An open \*gorm.DB with the model's table migrated.
- model: Pointer to model struct.
- where: Where clause \(e.g., "status = ?" or "id \> ?"\).
- args: Arguments for where clause placeholders.
- updates: Map of column to new value.

Example:

```
zentests.DBUpdateBy(t, db, &User{}, "status = ?", "pending", map[string]any{"processed": true})
```

<a name="NewApp"></a>
## func NewApp

```go
func NewApp(t *testing.T, cfg ...fiber.Config) *fiber.App
```

NewApp creates a Fiber application for testing with automatic shutdown registered via t.Cleanup, so the app is always stopped when the test finishes regardless of pass or fail. The app is created fresh on each call — no shared state between tests.

An optional \[fiber.Config\] can be passed to customize the app \(views engine, app name, middleware, error handler, etc.\). When no config is supplied the app is created with Fiber's defaults, identical to fiber.New\(\).

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance; marks this as a test helper and registers cleanup.
- cfg: Optional Fiber configuration. Only the first value is used if multiple are passed.

Returns:

- \*fiber.App: A fresh Fiber app ready for route registration.

Example — zero config:

```
func (s *MySuite) SetupTest() {
    s.app = zentests.NewApp(s.T())
    s.app.Get("/ping", handler)
}
```

Example — with views engine:

```
engine := html.New("./views", ".html")
 // register view helpers

	app := zentests.NewApp(t, fiber.Config{
	    Views:             engine,
	    AppName:           "MyApp",
	    PassLocalsToViews: true,
	})
```

<a name="SetHeader"></a>
## func SetHeader

```go
func SetHeader(key, value string) map[string]string
```

SetHeader creates a header map with a single key\-value pair. This is a utility function to help construct header maps for custom headers when using raw body request methods.

Parameters:

- key: The header name
- value: The header value

Returns:

- map\[string\]string: A map containing the single header

Example:

```
headers := zentests.SetHeader("Authorization", "Bearer token123")
// Use with a method that accepts headers parameter
```

<a name="SetupTestDB"></a>
## func SetupTestDB

```go
func SetupTestDB(t *testing.T) *gorm.DB
```

SetupTestDB opens a fresh in\-memory SQLite database configured for testing. The database uses silent logging to suppress GORM output during tests, and local time for all timestamp operations.

The connection is automatically closed when the test finishes via [testing.T.Cleanup](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T.Cleanup>), so no explicit teardown is required in the common case. Use [CloseTestDB](<#CloseTestDB>) only when you need to close the connection before the test ends \(e.g. to test reconnect behavior\).

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance; marks this as a test helper and registers cleanup.

Returns:

- \*gorm.DB: A connected, empty database. No tables are created — use [SetupTestDBWithModels](<#SetupTestDBWithModels>) or [DBMigrate](<#DBMigrate>) to add schema.

Example:

```
db := zentests.SetupTestDB(t)
// db is connected; no tables yet
zentests.DBMigrate(t, db, &Post{})
```

<a name="SetupTestDBWithModels"></a>
## func SetupTestDBWithModels

```go
func SetupTestDBWithModels(t *testing.T, models ...any) *gorm.DB
```

SetupTestDBWithModels opens an in\-memory SQLite database and runs AutoMigrate for every provided model in a single call. This is the most common entry point for database tests — it replaces the three\-line open/migrate/check sequence with one line.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance.
- models: One or more pointers to GORM model structs \(e.g. &User\{\}, &Post\{\}\).

Returns:

- \*gorm.DB: A connected database with the requested tables created.

Example — suite\-level setup, data reset between tests:

```
func (s *MySuite) SetupSuite() {
    s.db = zentests.SetupTestDBWithModels(s.T(), &User{}, &Post{})
}

func (s *MySuite) SetupTest() {
    zentests.DBReset(s.T(), s.db)
}
```

<a name="DefaultLogger"></a>
## type DefaultLogger

DefaultLogger is a production\-ready [Logger](<#Logger>) implementation backed by the standard library's log package. All output is written to stderr with level prefixes: "DEBUG: ", "WARN: ", or "FATAL: ".

Fatalf calls [os.Exit](<https://pkg.go.dev/os/#Exit>)\(1\) after logging. The exit behaviour can be overridden via the unexported exitFn field, which is only used in tests for the DefaultLogger itself.

Example:

```
var log zentests.Logger = zentests.DefaultLogger{}
log.Warnf("retrying in %d seconds", 5)
```

```go
type DefaultLogger struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="DefaultLogger.Debugf"></a>
### func \(DefaultLogger\) Debugf

```go
func (l DefaultLogger) Debugf(format string, v ...any)
```

Debugf logs a formatted debug message prefixed with "DEBUG: ".

<a name="DefaultLogger.Fatalf"></a>
### func \(DefaultLogger\) Fatalf

```go
func (l DefaultLogger) Fatalf(format string, v ...any)
```

Fatalf logs a formatted fatal message prefixed with "FATAL: " then exits with code 1. NOTE: uses Printf internally \(not [log.Fatalf](<https://pkg.go.dev/log/#Fatalf>)\) so the exit is handled by exitFn, making it safe to test without actually terminating the process.

<a name="DefaultLogger.Warnf"></a>
### func \(DefaultLogger\) Warnf

```go
func (l DefaultLogger) Warnf(format string, v ...any)
```

Warnf logs a formatted warning message prefixed with "WARN: ".

<a name="FileUpload"></a>
## type FileUpload

FileUpload describes one file in a PostMultipart request.

```go
type FileUpload struct {
    // Name is the form field name. The same name may appear in several entries.
    Name string
    // Filename is the file name presented to the server.
    Filename string
    // Content is the file's bytes.
    Content []byte
}
```

<a name="Jar"></a>
## type Jar

Jar sends requests to one Fiber app and remembers every cookie the app sets, the way a browser does. It lets a test flow span several requests, such as login, CSRF checks and session tests. Each request returns a \*Response, so the usual assertions compose with jar requests.

Not an RFC 6265 cookie jar. It is deliberately a flat map of name to value:

- No Path or Domain matching. A cookie is sent with every request to the app.
- No Secure or HttpOnly enforcement. Check those attributes with Response.Cookie.
- No Expires\-based expiry. Only the MaxAge \< 0 or empty\-value deletion rule applies.
- A cookie set to "" is indistinguishable from a deletion, so the empty\-value rule wins.

Jar is not safe for concurrent use. Tests using it run on a single goroutine.

Example:

```
jar := zentests.NewJar(t, app)
csrf := jar.Get("/login").OK().BodyString()
jar.PostForm("/login", url.Values{"csrf": {csrf}, "user": {"jane"}}).Status(302)
jar.Get("/settings").OK().Contains("Welcome Jane")
```

```go
type Jar struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="NewJar"></a>
### func NewJar

```go
func NewJar(t testing.TB, app *fiber.App) *Jar
```

NewJar returns an empty Jar for app. It fails the test when app is nil.

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.TB](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#TB>) instance for assertions
- app: The Fiber application to test against; must not be nil

Returns:

- \*Jar: A Jar holding no cookies

Example:

```
jar := zentests.NewJar(t, app)
```

<a name="Jar.Cookie"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) Cookie

```go
func (j *Jar) Cookie(name string) string
```

Cookie returns the value the jar holds for name, or "" when there is none. It never fails the test, so it can check that a cookie is absent.

Parameters:

- name: The cookie name

Returns:

- string: The stored cookie value, or "" when absent

Example:

```
if jar.Cookie("session") == "" { t.Fatal("no session") }
```

<a name="Jar.Get"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) Get

```go
func (j *Jar) Get(path string) *Response
```

Get sends a GET request to path with the stored cookies.

Parameters:

- path: The request path \(e.g., "/login"\)

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
jar.Get("/settings").OK()
```

<a name="Jar.PostForm"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) PostForm

```go
func (j *Jar) PostForm(path string, values url.Values) *Response
```

PostForm sends a POST request to path with values encoded as application/x\-www\-form\-urlencoded, together with the stored cookies.

Parameters:

- path: The request path \(e.g., "/login"\)
- values: The form fields; keys and values are escaped and multi\-value safe

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
jar.PostForm("/login", url.Values{"user": {"jane"}}).Status(302)
```

<a name="Jar.PostMultipart"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) PostMultipart

```go
func (j *Jar) PostMultipart(path string, fields map[string]string, files []FileUpload) *Response
```

PostMultipart sends a POST request with multipart/form\-data and the stored cookies, typically for file uploads. See T.PostMultipart for the FileUpload fields.

Parameters:

- path: The request path \(e.g., "/upload"\)
- fields: Plain form fields \(nil when there are none\)
- files: The files to upload \(nil when there are none\)

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
jar.PostMultipart("/upload", nil, []zentests.FileUpload{
    {Name: "file", Filename: "a.txt", Content: []byte("hello")},
}).OK()
```

<a name="Jar.Send"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) Send

```go
func (j *Jar) Send(req *http.Request) *Response
```

Send sends a caller\-built request with the stored cookies, then stores the cookies the response sets. Use it as an escape hatch when Get and PostForm do not fit.

Parameters:

- req: The request to send; its own cookies are kept and the stored ones are added

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodDelete, "/session", nil)
jar.Send(req).NoContent()
```

<a name="Jar.SetHeader"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) SetHeader

```go
func (j *Jar) SetHeader(key, value string)
```

SetHeader sets a default header that is sent with every request made through the jar. A header already on the request, such as PostForm's Content\-Type, takes precedence over a default with the same name. Header names are canonicalized, so "x\-api\-key" and "X\-Api\-Key" configure the same default.

Parameters:

- key: The header name \(e.g., "Accept"\)
- value: The header value

Example:

```
jar := zentests.NewJar(t, app)
jar.SetHeader("Accept", "application/json")
```

<a name="Jar.WithBearer"></a>
### func \(\*Jar\) WithBearer

```go
func (j *Jar) WithBearer(token string)
```

WithBearer sets the default Authorization header to "Bearer \<token\>", which is sent with every request made through the jar.

Parameters:

- token: The bearer token

Example:

```
jar := zentests.NewJar(t, app)
jar.WithBearer(token)
```

<a name="Logger"></a>
## type Logger

Logger defines the minimal logging interface for use with zentests\-compatible packages. It allows the host application to inject a logger for debug messages, warnings, and fatal errors. Implement this interface in your own code, then inject a [MockLogger](<#MockLogger>) in tests to capture and assert on log output without any side effects.

Example — production code:

```
type MyService struct {
    log zentests.Logger
}
```

Example — test code:

```
ml := &zentests.MockLogger{}
svc := MyService{log: ml}
svc.DoSomething()
s.True(ml.WarnCalled)
```

```go
type Logger interface {
    // Debugf logs a formatted debug message.
    Debugf(format string, v ...any)

    // Warnf logs a formatted warning message (non-fatal).
    Warnf(format string, v ...any)

    // Fatalf logs a formatted fatal error message and terminates the process.
    Fatalf(format string, v ...any)
}
```

<a name="MockLogger"></a>
## type MockLogger

MockLogger is an exported test double that implements [Logger](<#Logger>) by capturing all log calls without any side effects. Inject \*MockLogger into code\-under\-test, then inspect the exported fields in assertions.

Example:

```
func (s *MySuite) Test_Warns_On_Missing_Config() {
    ml := &zentests.MockLogger{}
    svc := NewMyService(ml)
    svc.Start() // triggers Warnf internally
    s.True(ml.WarnCalled)
    s.Equal("config not found", ml.WarnMsg)
}
```

All three methods \(Debugf, Warnf, Fatalf\) set their respective \*Called and \*Msg fields. Fatalf does NOT call [os.Exit](<https://pkg.go.dev/os/#Exit>) — safe to use in tests.

```go
type MockLogger struct {
    // DebugCalled is true if Debugf was called at least once.
    DebugCalled bool
    // WarnCalled is true if Warnf was called at least once.
    WarnCalled bool
    // FatalCalled is true if Fatalf was called at least once.
    FatalCalled bool

    // DebugMsg holds the last formatted message passed to Debugf.
    DebugMsg string
    // WarnMsg holds the last formatted message passed to Warnf.
    WarnMsg string
    // FatalMsg holds the last formatted message passed to Fatalf.
    FatalMsg string
}
```

<a name="MockLogger.Debugf"></a>
### func \(\*MockLogger\) Debugf

```go
func (m *MockLogger) Debugf(format string, v ...any)
```

Debugf records the call and formatted message. Does not produce any output.

<a name="MockLogger.Fatalf"></a>
### func \(\*MockLogger\) Fatalf

```go
func (m *MockLogger) Fatalf(format string, v ...any)
```

Fatalf records the call and formatted message. Does NOT call [os.Exit](<https://pkg.go.dev/os/#Exit>) — safe in tests.

<a name="MockLogger.Warnf"></a>
### func \(\*MockLogger\) Warnf

```go
func (m *MockLogger) Warnf(format string, v ...any)
```

Warnf records the call and formatted message. Does not produce any output.

<a name="Response"></a>
## type Response

Response wraps an HTTP response with fluent assertion methods. It provides a chainable API for making assertions on HTTP responses including status codes, headers, body content, and JSON data. The response body is lazily loaded when first accessed to avoid unnecessary reads.

Response maintains internal state including the parsed JSON body and tracks whether the body has been read to prevent multiple reads from the response stream.

Fields:

- t: The [testing.TB](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#TB>) instance for making assertions
- StatusCode: The HTTP status code from the response
- Header: The HTTP headers from the response
- resp: The underlying \[http.Response\]
- body: The cached response body bytes \(lazy loaded\)
- bodyRead: Flag indicating if body has been read
- parsed: Flag indicating if JSON parsing has been attempted
- parsedJSON: The parsed JSON body as a map \(cached after first parse\)

```go
type Response struct {
    Header http.Header

    StatusCode int
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Response.Accepted"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Accepted

```go
func (r *Response) Accepted() *Response
```

Accepted asserts that the HTTP status code is 202 \(Accepted\). Convenience method equivalent to Status\(202\). Indicates the request has been accepted for processing but not completed.

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.PostJSON(app, "/jobs", jobData).Accepted()
```

<a name="Response.ArrayContains"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) ArrayContains

```go
func (r *Response) ArrayContains(path string, expected any) *Response
```

ArrayContains asserts that the value at path is an array holding an element equal to the expected value. Numeric expectations follow Has: any Go numeric type matches a JSON number. Object and array expectations must be written in decoded form, with JSON numbers as float64; use Has on a "path.index" path to check a nested object.

Parameters:

- path: The JSON key path using dot notation
- expected: The element the array must contain

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/api/users/1").ArrayContains("user.roles", "admin")
```

<a name="Response.ArrayEmpty"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) ArrayEmpty

```go
func (r *Response) ArrayEmpty(path string) *Response
```

ArrayEmpty asserts that the value at path is an array with no elements. Fails when the path does not exist or is not an array.

Parameters:

- path: The JSON key path using dot notation

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/api/users/1").ArrayEmpty("user.roles")
```

<a name="Response.ArrayLength"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) ArrayLength

```go
func (r *Response) ArrayLength(path string, expected int) *Response
```

ArrayLength asserts that the JSON key is an array with the expected length.

Parameters:

- path: The JSON key path using dot notation
- expected: The expected array length

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/api/users").ArrayLength("data.users", 10)
```

<a name="Response.BadRequest"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) BadRequest

```go
func (r *Response) BadRequest() *Response
```

BadRequest asserts that the HTTP status code is 400 \(Bad Request\). Convenience method equivalent to Status\(400\). Indicates the server cannot process the request due to client error.

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.PostJSON(app, "/users", invalidData).BadRequest()
```

<a name="Response.Bind"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Bind

```go
func (r *Response) Bind(target any) *Response
```

Bind decodes the response body into target with encoding/json, so a test can work with typed values instead of dot\-notation paths. It reads the raw body, not the JSON\(\) cache. Fails the test when the body is not valid JSON for the target, and still returns the receiver for chaining.

Parameters:

- target: The value to decode into; typically a pointer to a struct or map

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
var user struct {
    ID   int    `json:"id"`
    Name string `json:"name"`
}
zt.Get(app, "/api/users/1").OK().Bind(&user)
```

<a name="Response.Body"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Body

```go
func (r *Response) Body() []byte
```

Body returns the response body as bytes. The body is lazily loaded on first call and cached for subsequent accesses. This prevents multiple reads from the response stream which would return empty.

Returns:

- \[\]byte: The response body as bytes

Example:

```
body := resp.Body()
fmt.Println(string(body))
```

<a name="Response.BodyMatches"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) BodyMatches

```go
func (r *Response) BodyMatches(pattern string) *Response
```

BodyMatches asserts that the response body matches the regex pattern. Useful for validating dynamic content or complex text patterns.

Parameters:

- pattern: The regex pattern to match against the body

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/users/1").BodyMatches(`User ID: \d+`)
```

<a name="Response.BodyString"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) BodyString

```go
func (r *Response) BodyString() string
```

BodyString returns the response body as a string. Convenience method that converts Body\(\) bytes to string.

Returns:

- string: The response body as a string

Example:

```
bodyStr := resp.BodyString()
assert.Contains(t, bodyStr, "success")
```

<a name="Response.Contains"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Contains

```go
func (r *Response) Contains(substring string) *Response
```

Contains asserts that the response body contains the specified substring. Case\-sensitive substring search in the response body.

Parameters:

- substring: The substring to search for in the body

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/page").Contains("Welcome")
```

<a name="Response.Cookie"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Cookie

```go
func (r *Response) Cookie(name string) *http.Cookie
```

Cookie returns the named cookie from the response, failing the test when it was not set. Use it to check attributes the [Jar](<#Jar>) does not keep, such as HttpOnly, Path, Secure and SameSite.

Parameters:

- name: The cookie name

Returns:

- \*\[http.Cookie\]: The parsed Set\-Cookie entry with its attributes

Example:

```
cookie := zt.Get(app, "/login").OK().Cookie("session")
assert.True(t, cookie.HttpOnly)
```

<a name="Response.CookieHasValues"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) CookieHasValues

```go
func (r *Response) CookieHasValues(expected map[string]string) *Response
```

CookieHasValues asserts that response cookies match the expected values. Parses all Set\-Cookie headers and verifies each cookie name\-value pair.

Parameters:

- expected: Map of cookie names to expected values

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/settings").CookieHasValues(map[string]string{
    "lang": "en",
    "theme": "dark",
})
```

<a name="Response.CookieNotPresent"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) CookieNotPresent

```go
func (r *Response) CookieNotPresent(name string) *Response
```

CookieNotPresent asserts that the response did not set a cookie with the given name. A deletion cookie \(empty value or MaxAge \< 0\) does not fail this check; use the Jar to check that a cookie is gone.

Parameters:

- name: The cookie name

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/public").OK().CookieNotPresent("session")
```

<a name="Response.Created"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Created

```go
func (r *Response) Created() *Response
```

Created asserts that the HTTP status code is 201 \(Created\). Convenience method equivalent to Status\(201\). Typically used after POST requests that create new resources.

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.PostJSON(app, "/users", data).Created()
```

<a name="Response.Debug"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Debug

```go
func (r *Response) Debug() *Response
```

Debug prints detailed response information to stdout for troubleshooting. Outputs status code, headers, body, and parsed JSON \(if available\). Sensitive headers such as Authorization and Set\-Cookie are redacted. This is useful during test development to inspect response details. Returns the receiver for method chaining.

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/users").Debug().OK()
```

<a name="Response.Dump"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Dump

```go
func (r *Response) Dump() string
```

Dump returns raw response details as a formatted string. Useful for custom logging or including response details in test failure messages. Unlike Debug\(\), this returns a string instead of printing to stdout. Sensitive headers such as Authorization and Set\-Cookie are redacted.

Returns:

- string: Formatted string with status, headers, and body

Example:

```
details := resp.Dump()
t.Logf("Response details: %s", details)
```

<a name="Response.Equals"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Equals

```go
func (r *Response) Equals(expected string) *Response
```

Equals asserts that the response body equals the exact expected string. Performs an exact string comparison of the entire body.

Parameters:

- expected: The expected body content

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/ping").Equals("pong")
```

<a name="Response.Has"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) Has

```go
func (r *Response) Has(path string, expected any) *Response
```

Has asserts that the JSON key equals the expected value. Supports dot notation for nested keys. Fails if the key doesn't exist or if the value differs. Any Go numeric type \(int, float32, ...\) is accepted for numbers and compared as float64, because JSON numbers always decode to float64. Other types must match exactly.

Parameters:

- path: The JSON key path using dot notation
- expected: The expected value

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/api/users/1").Has("data.user.name", "John")
zt.Get(app, "/api/count").Has("data.count", 42) // any numeric type works
```

```go
func (r *Response) HasBool(path string, expected bool) *Response
```

HasBool asserts that the JSON key equals the expected boolean value.

Parameters:

- path: The JSON key path using dot notation
- expected: The expected boolean value

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/api/status").HasBool("data.active", true)
```

```go

```

HasContentType asserts that the Content\-Type header equals the expected value. Performs an exact match on the Content\-Type header.

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

<a name="Response.HasCookie"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) HasCookie

```go
func (r *Response) HasCookie(name string) *Response
```

HasCookie asserts that the response set a cookie with the given name, with any value. Use Cookie to read the cookie's attributes, or CookieHasValues to check its value. A deletion cookie \(empty value or MaxAge \< 0\) does not count as set; use the Jar to check that a stored cookie is gone.

Parameters:

- name: The cookie name

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/login").OK().HasCookie("session")
```

<a name="Response.HasFloat"></a>
### func \(\*Response\) HasFloat

```go
func (r *Response) HasFloat(path string, expected float64) *Response
```

HasFloat asserts that the JSON key equals the expected float64 value. Uses InDelta for comparison to handle floating point precision issues.

Parameters:

- expected: The expected float64 value

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining


Returns:


```go

```

JSONHasValues asserts that each listed key path holds its expected value. This is a subset check: keys that are not listed are ignored. Each entry is checked with Has, so the same type rules apply. Keys are checked in sorted order, so failures are reported in a stable order.

Parameters:

- expected: Map of key paths to expected values

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.Get(app, "/api/users/1").JSONHasValues(map[string]any{
    "data.user.name":   "John",
    "data.user.active": true,
})
```

```go

```

JSONMatches is an alias for JSONHasValues. It is a subset check: it asserts that each listed key path holds its expected value, and ignores any other keys in the body.

Deprecated: use JSONHasValues, which has the same behavior under a clearer name. JSONMatches is kept so existing tests keep compiling.

Parameters:

- expected: Map of key paths to expected values

Returns:

- \*Response: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

<a name="SuiteContext"></a>
## type SuiteContext

SuiteContext holds hooks and state for a BDD\-style describe block. Provides lifecycle hooks \(BeforeEach, AfterEach\) for test setup and teardown. Each describe block gets its own SuiteContext to manage test isolation.

Describe blocks can be nested. Hooks of enclosing blocks apply to tests in nested blocks: BeforeEach hooks run outermost first, and AfterEach hooks run innermost first.

Hooks are captured when It\(\) is called, so BeforeEach and AfterEach must be declared before the It\(\) calls they should apply to.

Fields:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance for running subtests
- parent: The enclosing SuiteContext, or nil for a top\-level block
- beforeEach: Function to run before each test case in the suite
- afterEach: Function to run after each test case in the suite

```go
type SuiteContext struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="SuiteContext.AfterEach"></a>
### func \(\*SuiteContext\) AfterEach

```go
func (ctx *SuiteContext) AfterEach(fn func(*T)) *SuiteContext
```

AfterEach sets the teardown hook function to run after each test case. Use this for cleanup like closing database connections or shutting down apps. Must be called before the It\(\) calls it should apply to. Returns the SuiteContext for method chaining.

Parameters:

- fn: Function to execute after each test case, receives \*T

Returns:

- \*SuiteContext: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
ctx.AfterEach(func(zt *zentests.T) {
    app.Shutdown()
    db.Cleanup()
})
```

<a name="SuiteContext.BeforeEach"></a>
### func \(\*SuiteContext\) BeforeEach

```go
func (ctx *SuiteContext) BeforeEach(fn func(*T)) *SuiteContext
```

BeforeEach sets the setup hook function to run before each test case. Use this for common setup like creating fresh app instances or test data. Must be called before the It\(\) calls it should apply to. Returns the SuiteContext for method chaining with AfterEach.

Parameters:

- fn: Function to execute before each test case, receives \*T

Returns:

- \*SuiteContext: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
ctx.BeforeEach(func(zt *zentests.T) {
    app = fiber.New()
    SetupRoutes(app)
}).AfterEach(func(zt *zentests.T) {
    app.Shutdown()
})
```

<a name="SuiteContext.Describe"></a>
### func \(\*SuiteContext\) Describe

```go
func (ctx *SuiteContext) Describe(name string, fn func(ctx *SuiteContext))
```

Describe creates a nested describe block inside this one. Hooks declared in the enclosing block apply to the tests in the nested block.

Parameters:

- name: The descriptive name for the nested group
- fn: Function that receives the nested SuiteContext

Example:

```
zt.Describe("Users", func(ctx *zentests.SuiteContext) {
    ctx.BeforeEach(func(zt *zentests.T) { app = setupTestApp() })

    ctx.Describe("when logged in", func(ctx *zentests.SuiteContext) {
        ctx.It("lists users", func(zt *zentests.T) {
            zt.Get(app, "/users").OK()
        })
    })
})
```

<a name="SuiteContext.It"></a>
### func \(\*SuiteContext\) It

```go
func (ctx *SuiteContext) It(name string, fn func(*T))
```

It runs a test case within a describe block. Runs the BeforeEach hooks of this block and its enclosing blocks, then fn, then the AfterEach hooks. AfterEach hooks are registered with t.Cleanup, so they still run when the test stops early \(for example through require\). Each It\(\) call creates a sub\-test that runs independently.

Parameters:

- name: The descriptive name for the test case \(e.g., "returns user list"\)
- fn: The test function receiving a \*T for making requests

Example:

```
ctx.It("returns user list", func(zt *zentests.T) {
    zt.Get(app, "/users").OK().IsJSON()
})
```

<a name="T"></a>
## type T

T wraps [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) with additional context for testing Fiber applications. It provides a fluent API for making HTTP requests against a Fiber app in tests. Request methods take the Fiber app explicitly; T also carries default headers and the testing context for chainable assertions.

Basic usage:

```
func TestEndpoint(t *testing.T) {
    zt := zentests.New(t)
    zt.Get(app, "/users").Status(200)
}
```

Fields:

- T: The embedded [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance for standard Go test functionality
- headers: Default headers sent with every request \(see SetHeader\)

```go
type T struct {
    *testing.T
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func New

```go
func New(t *testing.T) *T
```

New creates a new zentests context wrapping the provided [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>). This is the main entry point for using zentests. Pass the Fiber app explicitly to request methods such as Get\(app, "/"\).

Parameters:

- t: The [testing.T](<https://pkg.go.dev/testing/#T>) instance from your test function

Returns:

- \*T: A new zentests context with no Fiber app configured

Example:

```
func TestExample(t *testing.T) {
    zt := zentests.New(t)
    app := fiber.New()
    // declare app routes

    zt.Get(app, "/").OK()
}
```

<a name="T.Describe"></a>
### func \(\*T\) Describe

```go
func (zt *T) Describe(name string, fn func(ctx *SuiteContext))
```

Describe creates a BDD\-style test group with lifecycle hooks. Organizes related tests under a descriptive name with optional setup/teardown. Similar to describe/it blocks in testing frameworks like RSpec or Mocha.

Parameters:

- name: The descriptive name for the test group \(e.g., "User API", "Auth Service"\)
- fn: Function that receives the SuiteContext and defines test cases using It\(\)

Example:

```
zt.Describe("User API", func(ctx *zentests.SuiteContext) {
    ctx.BeforeEach(func(zt *zentests.T) {
        // Setup fresh app before each test
        app = setupTestApp()
    })

    ctx.It("creates a user", func(zt *zentests.T) {
        zt.PostJSON(app, "/users", data).Created()
    })
})
```

<a name="T.Get"></a>
### func \(\*T\) Get

```go
func (zt *T) Get(app *fiber.App, path string) *Response
```

Get performs a GET request against the Fiber app. Returns a \*Response for chaining assertions. Use this for testing GET endpoints.

Parameters:

- app: The Fiber application to test against
- path: The request path \(e.g., "/api/users"\)

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
zt := zentests.New(t)
resp := zt.Get(app, "/users")
resp.OK().IsJSON().Has("data.users.0.name", "John")
```

<a name="T.GetQuery"></a>
### func \(\*T\) GetQuery

```go
func (zt *T) GetQuery(app *fiber.App, path string, query url.Values) *Response
```

GetQuery performs a GET request to path with query appended. The values are encoded with \[url.Values.Encode\], so characters such as "&", "=" and spaces reach the handler unchanged. When path already carries a query string, the values are appended after "&".

Parameters:

- app: The Fiber application to test against
- path: The request path, with or without a query string
- query: The query parameters \(nil or empty sends path unchanged plus "?"\)

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
zt.GetQuery(app, "/search", url.Values{"q": {"go & rust"}, "page": {"2"}}).OK()
```


GetWithConfig performs a GET request with custom TestConfig for timeout/behavior control. Use this when you need to customize test behavior beyond defaults.

Parameters:

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
zt.GetWithConfig(app, "/slow-endpoint", fiber.TestConfig{
    Timeout: 5 * time.Second,
}).OK()
```

<a name="T.HasRoute"></a>
### func \(\*T\) HasRoute

```go
func (zt *T) HasRoute(method, path string, app *fiber.App, msgAndArgs ...any) *T
```

HasRoute asserts that a route with the given HTTP method and path is registered in the Fiber app. The method is case\-insensitive. Returns the receiver for chaining.

This is useful in tests that verify route registration without making an actual HTTP request — for example, when testing that a router setup function wires up all expected endpoints.

Parameters:

- method: HTTP method to check \(e.g. "GET", "POST"\); case\-insensitive
- path: The exact route path as registered \(e.g. "/users/:id"\)
- app: The Fiber application to inspect
- msgAndArgs: Optional failure message and format arguments \(testify\-style\)

Returns:

- \*T: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt := zentests.New(t)
zt.HasRoute("GET", "/users", app, "user list route must be registered")
zt.HasRoute("POST", "/users", app).
    HasRoute("DELETE", "/users/:id", app)
```

<a name="T.NotHasRoute"></a>
### func \(\*T\) NotHasRoute

```go
func (zt *T) NotHasRoute(method, path string, app *fiber.App, msgAndArgs ...any) *T
```

NotHasRoute asserts that no route with the given HTTP method and path is registered in the Fiber app. The complement of HasRoute. Returns the receiver for chaining.

Parameters:

- method: HTTP method to check; case\-insensitive
- path: The route path to verify is absent
- app: The Fiber application to inspect
- msgAndArgs: Optional failure message and format arguments

Returns:

- \*T: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt.NotHasRoute("DELETE", "/users", app, "bulk delete must not be exposed").
    NotHasRoute("PATCH", "/users", app)
```

<a name="T.PostMultipart"></a>
### func \(\*T\) PostMultipart

```go
func (zt *T) PostMultipart(app *fiber.App, path string, fields map[string]string, files []FileUpload) *Response
```

PostMultipart performs a POST request with multipart/form\-data, typically for file uploads. The Content\-Type header carries the multipart boundary.

Parameters:

- app: The Fiber application to test against
- path: The request path \(e.g., "/upload"\)
- fields: Plain form fields \(nil when there are none\)
- files: The files to upload \(nil when there are none\)

Returns:

- \*Response: A Response wrapper for making assertions

Example:

```
zt.PostMultipart(app, "/upload", map[string]string{"note": "hi"}, []zentests.FileUpload{
    {Name: "file", Filename: "a.txt", Content: []byte("hello")},
}).OK()
```

<a name="T.SetHeader"></a>
### func \(\*T\) SetHeader

```go
func (zt *T) SetHeader(key, value string) *T
```

SetHeader sets a default header that is sent with every request made through zt. A header set for a single request, such as PostJSON's Content\-Type, takes precedence over a default with the same name. Header names are canonicalized, so "x\-api\-key" and "X\-Api\-Key" configure the same default.

Parameters:

- key: The header name \(e.g., "Accept"\)
- value: The header value

Returns:

- \*T: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```
zt := zentests.New(t).SetHeader("Accept", "application/json")
zt.Get(app, "/users").OK()
```


Use is retained for source compatibility and checks that app is not nil. Request methods still require app to be passed explicitly.

Returns:

- \*T: The receiver for method chaining

<a name="T.WithBearer"></a>
### func \(\*T\) WithBearer

```go
func (zt *T) WithBearer(token string) *T
```

WithBearer sets the default Authorization header to "Bearer \<token\>", which is sent with every request made through zt.

Parameters:

- token: The bearer token

Returns:

- \*T: The receiver for method chaining

Example:

```

zt.Get(app, "/users").OK()
```
